claim: Across all 19 graded runs in the corpus, the tuner role accounts for ~54% of total cost and the coder role for ~31%. The remaining five roles (setup / designer / judge / aggregator / manager) together account for ~15%.

support.implication: If routing must downgrade exactly one role to save money, downgrading the tuner has roughly 1.7x the impact of downgrading the coder, and an order of magnitude more impact than downgrading any other single role.

scope: All 7 tasks observed so far, across 3 models. Pattern is consistent across tasks — tuner is the largest cost center in every single run we have.
limitations: manager cost reports as $0; this is the persistent orchestrator and its API spend is masked by cache hits in the current accounting. Do not interpret '$0' as 'manager is free regardless of model'; we have not verified this against raw API logs.
Cost share is computed over single-model runs only. Mixing a cheap coder with an expensive tuner (or vice versa) may shift cache-hit patterns and change the per-role share.

legacy_scope.applies_to: v2 role surface (8 roles incl. tuner/manager)
